title: What was Amazonia-1?
hook: Designed, assembled, tested and operated in Brazil, but launched in India.
summary: Launched in 2021, Amazonia-1 was the first Earth-observation satellite designed, integrated, tested and operated by Brazil.

cardBlocks.text: On 28 February 2021, at 1:54 a.m. Brasília time, Brazil launched Amazonia-1, the first Earth-observation satellite designed, integrated, tested and operated by the country itself. It flew on the Indian PSLV-C51 rocket from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, India, after more than a decade of development.

The satellite belongs to the Amazonia Mission, set up to observe and monitor deforestation, especially in the Amazon, and farming across the country. It was the first built on the Multimission Platform, which INPE developed to serve several projects and cut costs.
Amazonia-1, launched in 2021, was the first Earth-observation satellite built and operated entirely by Brazil.

deepDiveBlocks.text: Brazil had no rocket big enough to put Amazonia-1 into orbit. And the Alcântara Launch Centre, set up for rockets the size of the 19.7-metre VLS, had no facilities for a rocket like India’s 44.4-metre PSLV.
The same rocket carried 18 other satellites, five from India and thirteen from the United States. Today, Amazonia-1 images help produce INPE’s daily deforestation alerts.

heroMedia.alt: Diagram of the Multimission Platform: the same service module, with solar panel and thrusters, can carry different payloads; on Amazonia-1, a camera that watches the forest.
